what: Strata SQ-15 on a TRUE single T4 (device-restricted), with drafting enabled
hardware: 2x Tesla T4 but restricted to gpu0 via --gpu 0 and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0

vram_after_load_mib.note: gpu1 at 0 confirms the restriction held; this is a real single-card result

findings: Drafting IS active on a single T4: 331 draft tokens, 128 accepted, 38.7% acceptance.
Single T4: 22.6 tok/s with drafting, vs 18.3 tok/s on 2xT4 auto-split without it.
Per-token cost is flat in N, which means BLOCK cost grows linearly: compute-bound, not memory-bound. The earlier memory-bound reading was wrong and is withdrawn below.
The 4.4x gap between measured block cost and the memory floor is the opportunity for our batched dequant GEMM, and it is larger than the first report claimed.
correction_to_prior_claim: The earlier note said spec decode is a 0.98x loss on sm75 and that the path to 60 tok/s must be bytes moved alone. That was based on a 2xT4 run whose auto-probe disabled drafting. A single-card run enables it and accepts 38.7% of drafts. Spec decode is viable on T4; the earlier negative was a configuration artifact, not a hardware limit.
gap: 22.6 measured against 60 target: 2.65x to close, on one card, with drafting already on.

cost_curve_reading.reasoning: Block cost grows linearly with N: 62.7 ms at N=2 rising to 940.5 ms at N=32, about 15x. A memory-bound verify would read the weights once per block, so block cost would stay near one decode step (44.2 ms at 22.6 tok/s) and per-token cost would fall roughly as 1/N. Instead per-token cost is flat, which is the signature of re-doing the dequant work for every token in the block.
cost_curve_reading.quantified_gap: An 8-token verify block measured 192.5 ms; the memory-bound ideal is 44.2 ms. That is 4.4x more compute than the memory floor allows, so Strata's sm75 path is spending about 4x too much on dequant per verified token.
cost_curve_reading.corroboration: Prefill at 26.4 tok/s on one T4 is far too slow for a memory-bound path. Prefill batches tokens the same way verify does, so a slow prefill and a linear block cost point at the same cause.

withdrawn_claims.claim: Per-token cost is FLAT in N (24-31 ms from N=2 to N=32). That is the memory-bound signature... the batched-dequant hypothesis has empirical support from Strata's own engine.
withdrawn_claims.why: Flat per-token cost means block cost grows with N, which is compute-bound. The numbers were right; the interpretation was backwards. Corrected by cross-checking against the memory floor (44.2 ms per decode step) and the prefill rate.
